comment: The whole extension world of the eTamil IDE. There is no marketplace in the
branded build, so what is listed here is what exists — three installed with
the IDE and four the developer can turn on.
Everything is fetched from Open VSX rather than Microsoft's gallery, whose
terms do not cover non-Microsoft builds and which an air-gapped bank could
not reach anyway. Versions are pinned so a build is reproducible; refresh

installed.title: eTamil
installed.why: The language itself: grammar, snippets, hovers, run, compile-on-type — all generated from lexer.rs.

installed.title: paRY
installed.why: The assistant. Its chat opens on the right.

installed.title: eTamil Dark
installed.why: The IDE's own colours. A built-in in the branded build, so it does not appear as something a developer installed.

installed.title: GitHub
installed.why: Pull requests and issues in the editor. The GitHub extension people mean when they say GitHub.

optional.title: Rust
optional.why: The Rust language server. The eTamil compiler is Rust, so this is for working on the language itself.

optional.title: Python
optional.why: The canonical Python extension, and it is on Open VSX under MIT.

optional.title: Node.js
optional.why: ESLint. Node debugging is already built into the editor, so the useful thing to add for JavaScript work is the linter rather than a runtime extension.

optional.title: React
optional.why: React snippets for JSX and hooks.
